# The Galois/Frobenius side-channel family is a FIFTH primitive — and it is closed three ways (an audit finding: entirely absent from the factoring record)

**Origin:** the round-33 audit measured that **145 of 185 factoring-relevant catalog
modules were never read** in 32 prior rounds. This note harvests the largest coherent
unread block — the **Galois/Frobenius residue-type side-channel family** — and reports
what it contains. The family is a genuine **candidate fifth primitive** alongside the
record's four (congruence-of-squares, order, smoothness/index-calculus, algebraic/CM), and
it is machine-checked **closed three independent ways**. It is a rigorous *negative*
result about a whole route family — and it was sitting unopened on disk the entire time.

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound** (never a floor). A kill is success. All theorem names
below were read from the actual Lean files (Rule 5); the record (`RESEARCH.md`, 9,771
lines) contains **zero** occurrences of the family — verified by grep.

## The family (the unread modules)

- `Cryptography/NonabelianTypeChannel/{GroupChannel, SplitType, Semiprime, Completeness,
  Entropy, Fields}.lean` — the **type channel**: the splitting type (factorisation shape)
  of `p` in a number field, read as the cycle type of Frobenius.
- `Combinatorics/D12SemiprimeWhichFactorWall.lean`,
  `Bridges/CyclicCubicWhichFactor.lean` — the **which-factor wall**.
- `Algebra/{ECMParityFrobenius, ECMParitySymmetric}.lean`,
  `Novelty/CmEcmOrder*.lean`, `Shared/ECMStage1OrderCompletion.lean` — **CM-ECM order
  shadows** and ECM stage-1 order completion.
- `Speculative/AutoResearch/ResidueChannelNonabelianTorsor.lean`,
  `Bridges/ResidueLeakageTorsorTriviality.lean` — the **Artin-symbol / torsor** channel;
  conjecture C5′ settled.

## Closure 1 — the abelianization cap (`typeChannel_le_logb_index`)

For a finite Galois group `S`, derived subgroup `N = [S,S]`, coset readout `c`, and **any**
splitting-type readout `T`:

> `mutualInfo S c T ≤ log₂ [S : N] = log₂|G^ab|`.

The proof is two lines: `mutualInfo ≤ H(c)` (info can't exceed the coarser variable) and
`H(coset) = log₂[S:N]` (Lagrange). It is airtight and general. Exact prime-level values
(`Fields.lean`): `S₃ = 1`, `S₄ = 1`, `A₄ = log₂3`, `D₄ = 2`, `V₄ = 2`, `C₄ = 2` bits. So a
five-type `S₄` field still cannot push more than **one bit** through a residue channel.
Perfect groups leak exactly zero (`typeChannel_eq_zero_of_perfect`).

## Closure 2 — the which-factor wall is an EXACT zero (`whichFactor_wall`)

For the semiprime `N = pq` with factors in an asymmetric box, knowing *which* factor
carried which splitting type adds **exactly zero bits** to *every* swap-invariant readout:

> `uEnt (asym n) (whichFactor n) = 1 ∧ mutInfo (asym n) (whichFactor n) k = 0`
> for every `k` with `k p.swap = k p`.

The zero is **exact, not a bound** (`mutInfo_eq_zero_of_flip`: a flip-invariance argument,
not an estimate). It is non-vacuous: the *ordered* readout does carry information
(`whichFactor_ordered_full`). So a Frobenius reader cannot learn which factor is which.

## Closure 3 — the Artin/torsor channel prunes nothing (`nonabelian_no_pruning`)

Conjecture C5′ asked whether the non-abelian Artin-symbol channel gives a *proper* fibre
(the first residue-type channel with nonzero pruning). It does not, and the reason is
sharper than a counting bound:

> In **any** group, for any target `σ` and any candidate `p`, the element
> `q = p⁻¹σ` compensates. So the fibre projects onto **every** conjugacy class.

Hence the Artin channel prunes **exactly zero** candidates, abelianian or not. The
pruning half of C5′ is false.

## What is NOT closed (the honest seams)

1. **The cap bounds the RESIDUE content, not the full type.** `I(coset;T) ≤ log₂[G:G']`;
   a readout not factoring through the abelianization coset is bounded only by `H(T)`. A
   higher-rank non-abelian `G` with large `log₂[G:G']` **and** a positive ordered-vs-
   unordered `I₂` gap is not excluded in principle.
2. **The wall's hypothesis is symmetry.** Every wall theorem assumes the readout is a
   function of `N` (or swap-invariant). A readout of an **asymmetric side-input** is
   untouched by the wall — though nothing yet supplies such a side-input computable from
   `N`.
3. **Distributional assumptions** (Rule 6): some semiprime figures rest on Chebotarev-type
   models that are conjectural, not measured.

Any new method from this family must, as a **conjunction**: supply a readout of `p` that
(i) does not factor through `G^ab`, (ii) breaks the swap symmetry, and (iii) yields more
than `O(1)` bits about which factor is which — all from `N` alone. No such readout is known.

## Significance

- The record's four-primitive census **needs amendment**: a fifth primitive exists (the
  Galois/Frobenius side channel) and is now **rigorously closed**, with an abelianization
  cap, an exact which-factor wall, and a no-pruning torsor law. This is a *stronger and
  more general* barrier than anything the record holds on this family — because the
  record does not hold anything on it at all.
- It is also a template for the **145-module audit**: the campaign's largest single failure
  was not a wrong idea but an **unread theorem**. The lesson generalises — before
  proposing a route, check whether it is already machine-checked on disk.

            ## v19 Research Core Methodology — Speculative Scientific-Method Loop

You are the Principal Investigator leading a speculative research team with four
roles: **Hypothesizer**, **Experimenter**, **Analyst**, and **Critic**. This engine
is configured for **Speculative Specifying (Bold Conjectures)**: target high-risk,
high-reward, grand-challenge level research while maintaining adversarial rigor.

### Stage 1 — Hypothesize (team: Hypothesizer)
Brainstorm 5–7 falsifiable conjectures about the topic. At least three must be
bold, surprising, or grand-challenge level. Rank them by expected scientific
impact, not by ease of proof.
**CRITICAL SCORING REQUIREMENT**: To maximize your Phase A quality score, your
conjectures MUST aim for extreme `proof_depth` (deep structural hierarchies rather
than shallow one-liners) and `cross_domain` bridging (combining distinct areas of
math, e.g., algebra with topology, or geometry with combinatorics).

### Stage 2 — Experiment (team: Experimenter)
For each conjecture, attempt to prove it in Lean 4 or disprove it with a concrete
counterexample. Prioritize the boldest conjectures first. If a proof is beyond
reach, prove the strongest lemma you can and mark the remaining step with exactly
one `sorry` that is clearly documented.

### Stage 3 — Analyze (team: Analyst)
Summarize what survived, what failed, and **why** failures failed. Distinguish
"true but hard", "false", and "needs a different definition". Extract structural
patterns that could unify several observations.

### Stage 4 — Critique / Adversarial Review (team: Critic)
Before finalizing, challenge every theorem:
- Is any theorem trivial (True, definitional equality, `native_decide`)?
- Does every main theorem have 0 sorries?
- Do the results genuinely extend the attached catalog files?
- Are there hidden assumptions or corner cases that break the claim?
If you find a weakness, fix it or replace the theorem with a guarded version and
explain the boundary.

### Stage 5 — Synthesize (team: Principal Investigator)
Combine the verified results into clean, compiling Lean 4 files.
Write a `FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md` that lists 3–5 **bold, testable** conjectures
derived from Stage 3 and Stage 4. Each conjecture must include a
"The key insight is..." sentence and a "Why now?" justification.

ADDITIONALLY — machine-readable directions block (REQUIRED). In
FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md, after the prose sections, emit a fenced JSON
array named future_directions.json with one object per direction
(3–6 entries), each with exactly these keys:
```json
[{"title": "<short noun-phrase name, NOT a sentence>",
  "domain": "<one of: NumberTheory, Algebra, Geometry, Combinatorics, Computation, Physics, Probability, Cryptography, Logic, MachineLearning, Tropical, Bridges>",
  "description": "<2-4 sentences: the conjecture, the approach, why it matters>",
  "conjecture": "<the precise mathematical claim>",
  "test": "<how to test or formalize it>",
  "if_true": "<consequence if true>",
  "if_false": "<consequence if false>",

# Round 34 — Attacking the order-free balance: the M-leg is exponent-REDUNDANT, and the `m`-reuse is load-bearing

Seven fresh-frontier channels against the order-free balance that (round 33) pins Harvey's
`N^{1/5}`. **Zero new methods, zero exponents moved — but two genuine corrections to the
record and to #417/#418, and one transferable screening tool.**

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound**, never a floor. No unconditional superpolynomial
lower bound for factoring is known in any model. A kill is success.

## Headline 1 — the M-leg is exponent-REDUNDANT (a correction to the round-33 map)

Round 33 concluded `1/5` is pinned by the three-term order-free triangle
`{r·lg³N vs N^{1/4}r^{(-1/4)}lg³N} + {m·lg²N vs N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m)}`. Brute-force LP over the
three **N-exponent** terms `{BSGS interior N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m), pair family r, baby-step list
m}` gives minimax exactly `1/5`. The round-34 finding:

> Adding the M-leg `M^{1/2} = (N/r)^{1/4}`, or **deleting it entirely**, leaves the minimax
> at `1/5` — and it stays at `1/5` even when the M-leg is made **completely free**
> (constant-factor `M⁰`). The M-leg carries ~25% of the polylog-weighted budget at
> `N = 2^100` and is **arithmetically inert**.

So the smoothness-sieve term is a large-looking, zero-leverage term. This is the campaign's
diagnosed failure mode with the sign flipped: a term that *looks* load-bearing because it is
big is worth exactly nothing. **Correction to #418's "three co-leaders"** — the M-leg is a
co-leader only in polylog weight, not in exponent; the exponent is carried by the interior,
`r`, and `m` alone.

## Headline 2 — the m-reuse is load-bearing, not slack (experiment refuted the survivor)

The one channel to survive both refuters was `nonlegendre`: a "collapse coupling" that
removes the baby-step split to reinterpret the `(a,b)` grid via a product tree with
separable exponents (essentially Strassen's `N^{1/4}`, Harvey Prop 2.5 / Remark 2.6). A
ground-truth-verified pipeline (real NTT product trees, remainder-tree multievaluation) was
built and run:

> The mechanism is a **correct** factoring algorithm, but its dominant input-size exponent
> is **0.2500**, not `≤ 0.20`. The fitted penalty slope is `0.046–0.052` against the exact
> closed form `1/20 = 0.0500`, confirming an `N^{1/20}` penalty.

Interpretation: **dropping the baby-step split deletes the `m` term, degrading a 3-term
balance to a 2-term one.** The `m`-reuse (the zero-sum trade in `m`) is **load-bearing, not
slack** — a direct, experiment-backed statement about the record's core reuse mechanism. The
hunt's fabricated constant ("256") table is refuted by the fit.

## Headline 3 — the transferable tool: the "delete-a-term" LP screen

> **Screening rule.** In a minimax cost `max{term_1, …, term_k}`, a term is worth optimising
> **iff deleting it (or making it free) moves the minimax value.** A term that does not move
> the value is worthless regardless of its weight. Run this LP before spending a round on any
> term.

This is the round's most transferable artefact and costs an afternoon. It is in the same
family as the round-33 **slack-constraint lemma** and the **symmetric-readout vacuity lemma**
— a small set of general screening tools the campaign now carries.

## Other theorem-worthy facts

- **Any extreme of the gcd-reveal family is algebraically solvable.** `q = k(p−1) − 1` gives
  `kp² − (k+1)p − N = 0`, discriminant `≡ (2kp − (k+1))²` — one integer square root. More
  generally, in the gcd-reveal family the density-1 extreme is always the algebraically
  solvable case. (The `eulergap2` cross attempt died here: its surviving extreme is a
  closed-form quadratic with an exactly-square discriminant.)
- **General-exponent reveal identity.** `R(E) = d_p(q−1) + d_q(p−1) − 2 d_p d_q`, with
  `d_p = gcd(E, p−1)`, valid for **all** exponents `E`; it recovers `card_revealing` at
  `E = N−1`. Verified numerically. This generalises round 33's Euler-gap count from the single
  exponent `N−1` to arbitrary `E`.

## The next concrete target (untouched)

Round 33 attacked `r` (pair filter; killed on residue-uniformity). Round 34 showed `M` is
redundant and `m`-reuse is load-bearing. That leaves **the baby-step `m`-leg and the
`m`-dependent BSGS interior — the only two terms never attacked with a power-of-`N`
mechanism.** `m` is untouched. (Flagged per Rule 6: the proposed `T = N^{(1/2−δ)/5}` target
is unverified arithmetic — run the delete-a-term LP before committing a round.)

**Do NOT** spend a round on LLL/flatness over the UMW CRT lattice: the prefactoring kill
supersedes it — within that framework the `c=1` branch cannot reach `1/6` at any window size.

## Honest summary
Zero new factoring methods across 32 → 34 rounds — but the failures are now sharp,
non-repeating, and each round yields reusable general lemmas (slack-constraint, delete-a-term
LP, symmetric-readout vacuity) plus machine-checked corrections. The frontier is the
baby-step `m`-leg; the formally-open door remains the UMW covering.

/-- `gcd(E, r-1)·gcd(E, s-1) ≤ gcd(E, r-1)·(s-1)` for a prime `s`. -/
theorem gcd_mul_gcd_le (E r s : ℕ) (hs : s.Prime) :
    Nat.gcd E (r - 1) * Nat.gcd E (s - 1) ≤ Nat.gcd E (r - 1) * (s - 1) :=

theorem card_revealing_exp [Fact p.Prime] [Fact q.Prime] (E : ℕ) :
    Nat.card {v : (ZMod p)ˣ × (ZMod q)ˣ // v.1 ^ E = 1 ∧ ¬ v.2 ^ E = 1}
      + Nat.card {v : (ZMod p)ˣ × (ZMod q)ˣ // v.2 ^ E = 1 ∧ ¬ v.1 ^ E = 1}
      = Nat.gcd E (p - 1) * (q - 1) + Nat.gcd E (q - 1) * (p - 1)
          - 2 * (Nat.gcd E (p - 1) * Nat.gcd E (q - 1)) := by
  have hp : p.Prime := Fact.out
  have hq : q.Prime := Fact.out
  have h1 := gcd_mul_gcd_le E p q hq
  have h2 : Nat.gcd E (p - 1) * Nat.gcd E (q - 1) ≤ Nat.gcd E (q - 1) * (p - 1) := by
    rw [Nat.mul_comm]; exact gcd_mul_gcd_le E q p hp
  rw [card_reveal_left_exp, card_reveal_right_exp]
  omega

/-- **The identity recovers `card_revealing` at `E = N - 1`.** Both gcds collapse to
the Euler gap `g`, giving `g(q-1) + g(p-1) - 2g²`. -/
theorem card_revealing_exp_recovers [Fact p.Prime] [Fact q.Prime] :
    Nat.gcd (p * q - 1) (p - 1) * (q - 1) + Nat.gcd (p * q - 1) (q - 1) * (p - 1)
        - 2 * (Nat.gcd (p * q - 1) (p - 1) * Nat.gcd (p * q - 1) (q - 1))
      = eulerGap p q * (q - 1) + eulerGap p q * (p - 1) - 2 * (eulerGap p q) ^ 2 := by
  have hp : p.Prime := Fact.out
  have hq : q.Prime := Fact.out

theorem reveal_partition (P Q x y : ℕ) (hx : x ≤ P) (hy : y ≤ Q) :

  obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hx

/-- **★ Square discriminant.** If `q = k(p-1) + s` then `N = pq` satisfies

`(s-k)² + 4kN = (2kp + s - k)²`. -/

    (s - k) ^ 2 + 4 * k * (p * (k * (p - 1) + s)) = (2 * k * p + s - k) ^ 2 := by
  ring

/-- The quadratic relation itself. -/
theorem extreme_quadratic (p k s : ℤ) :
    k * p ^ 2 + (s - k) * p - p * (k * (p - 1) + s) = 0 := by ring

/-- **One integer square root factors the `s = 1` extreme.** If `q = k(p-1) + 1`
with `k ≥ 1`, `p ≥ 1`, then `Nat.sqrt((k-1)² + 4kN) = 2kp - (k-1)` and

theorem extreme_factor_by_sqrt (p k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
    (Nat.sqrt ((k - 1) ^ 2 + 4 * k * (p * (k * (p - 1) + 1))) + (k - 1)) / (2 * k) = p := by
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hk
  obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hp
  have hsq : (1 + k - 1) ^ 2 + 4 * (1 + k) * ((1 + p) * ((1 + k) * (1 + p - 1) + 1))
      = (2 * (1 + k) * p + k + 2) ^ 2 := by
    simp only [Nat.add_sub_cancel_left]; ring
  rw [hsq, Nat.sqrt_eq', Nat.add_sub_cancel_left]
  rw [show 2 * (1 + k) * p + k + 2 + k = (1 + p) * (2 * (1 + k)) by ring]
  exact Nat.mul_div_cancel _ (by omega)

/-- **One integer square root factors the `s = -1` extreme** (`q = k(p-1) - 1`, the
`eulergap2` case): `kp² - (k+1)p - N = 0` with discriminant `(2kp - (k+1))²`. -/
theorem extreme_factor_by_sqrt_neg (p k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hp : 2 ≤ p) :
    (Nat.sqrt ((k + 1) ^ 2 + 4 * k * (p * (k * (p - 1) - 1))) + (k + 1)) / (2 * k) = p := by
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hk
  obtain ⟨p, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hp
  have h1 : (1 + k) * (2 + p - 1) - 1 = k + p + k * p := by
    have : (1 + k) * (2 + p - 1) = 1 + (k + p + k * p) := by
      rw [show 2 + p - 1 = 1 + p by omega]; ring
    omega
  have hsq : (1 + k + 1) ^ 2 + 4 * (1 + k) * ((2 + p) * ((1 + k) * (2 + p - 1) - 1))
      = (2 * k * p + 2 * p + 3 * k + 2) ^ 2 := by
    rw [h1]; ring
  rw [hsq, Nat.sqrt_eq']
  rw [show 2 * k * p + 2 * p + 3 * k + 2 + (1 + k + 1) = (2 + p) * (2 * (1 + k)) by ring]
  exact Nat.mul_div_cancel _ (by omega)

/-- **★ The maximal-gap extreme reveals `(p-1)(q-p)` units and is solvable.**
If `(p-1) ∣ (q-1)` (Euler gap `g = p-1`, the largest it can be when `p < q`), the
reveal count is `(p-1)(q-p)` — a density `(q-p)/(q-1) = 1 - 1/k` tending to `1` —
and writing `q = k(p-1) + 1`, the factor `p` is returned by a single integer square
root.  The high-density end of the gcd-reveal family is the algebraically solvable
end. -/
theorem max_reveal_extreme [Fact p.Prime] [Fact q.Prime] (hpq : p < q)
    (hdvd : (p - 1) ∣ (q - 1)) :
    Nat.card {v : (ZMod p)ˣ × (ZMod q)ˣ //
        v.1 ^ (p * q - 1) = 1 ∧ ¬ v.2 ^ (p * q - 1) = 1}
      + Nat.card {v : (ZMod p)ˣ × (ZMod q)ˣ //
        v.2 ^ (p * q - 1) = 1 ∧ ¬ v.1 ^ (p * q - 1) = 1} = (p - 1) * (q - p) ∧
    (Nat.sqrt (((q - 1) / (p - 1) - 1) ^ 2 + 4 * ((q - 1) / (p - 1)) * (p * q))
        + ((q - 1) / (p - 1) - 1)) / (2 * ((q - 1) / (p - 1))) = p := by
  have hp : p.Prime := Fact.out
  have hq : q.Prime := Fact.out
  have hp2 := hp.two_le
  have hg : eulerGap p q = p - 1 := Nat.gcd_eq_left hdvd
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hdvd
  have hkpos : 1 ≤ k := by
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with h | h
    · subst h; omega
    · exact h
  have hkdiv : (q - 1) / (p - 1) = k := by
    rw [hk]; exact Nat.mul_div_cancel_left _ (by omega)
  have hqk : q = k * (p - 1) + 1 := by rw [Nat.mul_comm]; omega
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [card_revealing, hg]
    have hqp : q - 1 = (p - 1) + (q - p) := by omega
    rw [hqp, sq]
    have : (p - 1) * (p - 1 + (q - p)) + (p - 1) * (p - 1) = 2 * ((p - 1) * (p - 1))
        + (p - 1) * (q - p) := by ring
    omega
  · rw [hkdiv, hqk]
    exact extreme_factor_by_sqrt p k hkpos (by omega)

end AsymmetricExponent

/-! ## The general screening tool -/

/-- `c` is a lower bound for the minimax of `F` over the parameter space. -/
def MinimaxLB {X : Type*} (F : X → ℚ) (c : ℚ) : Prop := ∀ x, c ≤ F x

/-- `v` is the minimax value of `F`: a lower bound that is attained. -/
def IsMinimaxValue {X : Type*} (F : X → ℚ) (v : ℚ) : Prop :=
  MinimaxLB F v ∧ ∃ x, F x = v

/-- The minimax value is unique. -/
theorem IsMinimaxValue.unique {X : Type*} {F : X → ℚ} {v w : ℚ}
    (hv : IsMinimaxValue F v) (hw : IsMinimaxValue F w) : v = w := by
  obtain ⟨hv1, x, hx⟩ := hv
  obtain ⟨hw1, y, hy⟩ := hw
  have h1 := hv1 y
  have h2 := hw1 x
  linarith

/-- **★ THE DELETE-A-TERM SCREEN.** A lower bound `c` survives *every* choice of
the extra term `g'` — shrinking it, reshaping it, making it free — iff `c` is a
lower bound for the remaining terms `F'` alone.  So a term whose deletion does not
move the minimax is worth nothing to optimise, whatever its size. -/
theorem delete_a_term_screen {X : Type*} (F' : X → ℚ) (c : ℚ) :
    (∀ g' : X → ℚ, MinimaxLB (fun x => max (F' x) (g' x)) c) ↔ MinimaxLB F' c := by
  constructor
  · intro h x
    have := h F' x
    simpa using this
  · intro h g' x
    exact le_trans (h x) (le_max_left _ _)

/-- **The screen, positive form.** Some modification `g'` of a term brings the
minimax strictly below `v` iff deleting the term already does. -/
theorem term_worth_optimising_iff {X : Type*} (F' : X → ℚ) (v : ℚ) :
    (∃ g' : X → ℚ, ∃ x, max (F' x) (g' x) < v) ↔ ∃ x, F' x < v := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨g', x, hx⟩
    exact ⟨x, lt_of_le_of_lt (le_max_left _ _) hx⟩
  · rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
    exact ⟨F', x, by simpa using hx⟩

/-- **An inert term preserves the value.** If `v` is the minimax value of `F'`,
attained at `x₀`, and the extra term satisfies `g x₀ ≤ v`, then `max F' g` has
value exactly `v`. -/
theorem inert_term_preserves_value {X : Type*} (F' g : X → ℚ) (v : ℚ) (x₀ : X)
    (hlb : MinimaxLB F' v) (hx₀ : F' x₀ = v) (hg : g x₀ ≤ v) :
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x => max (F' x) (g x)) v :=
  ⟨fun x => le_trans (hlb x) (le_max_left _ _), x₀, by
    show max (F' x₀) (g x₀) = v
    rw [hx₀]; exact max_eq_left hg⟩

/-- **Adding a term never lowers a value** (monotonicity of the minimax). -/
theorem add_term_monotone {X : Type*} (F' g : X → ℚ) (v w : ℚ)
    (hF : IsMinimaxValue F' v) (hFg : IsMinimaxValue (fun x => max (F' x) (g x)) w) :
    v ≤ w := by
  obtain ⟨_, x, hx⟩ := hFg
  have := hF.1 x
  have h2 : F' x ≤ max (F' x) (g x) := le_max_left _ _
  linarith

  mleg_value_of_le _ (by norm_num)

/-- **The full parametric value above the breakpoint.** For `θ ≥ 1/4` the minimax
is exactly `θ/(1+θ)`, attained at `a = θ/(1+θ)`, `b = (1-a)/4`. -/
theorem mleg_value_of_ge (θ : ℚ) (hθ : 1 / 4 ≤ θ) :
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x : ℚ × ℚ => costM θ x.1 x.2) (θ / (1 + θ)) := by
  have hpos : (0 : ℚ) < 1 + θ := by linarith
  refine ⟨fun x => ?_, (θ / (1 + θ), (1 - θ / (1 + θ)) / 4), ?_⟩
  · show θ / (1 + θ) ≤ max (costExp x.1 x.2) (θ * (1 - x.1))
    rw [div_le_iff₀ hpos]
    have h1 : x.1 ≤ max (costExp x.1 x.2) (θ * (1 - x.1)) :=
      le_trans (le_max_left _ _) (le_max_left _ _)
    have h2 : θ * (1 - x.1) ≤ max (costExp x.1 x.2) (θ * (1 - x.1)) := le_max_right _ _
    nlinarith
  · show max (max (θ / (1 + θ)) (max ((1 - θ / (1 + θ)) / 4)
        (1 / 2 - θ / (1 + θ) / 2 - (1 - θ / (1 + θ)) / 4))) (θ * (1 - θ / (1 + θ)))
        = θ / (1 + θ)
    have e1 : 1 / 2 - θ / (1 + θ) / 2 - (1 - θ / (1 + θ)) / 4 = (1 - θ / (1 + θ)) / 4 := by
      ring
    have e2 : θ * (1 - θ / (1 + θ)) = θ / (1 + θ) := by
      field_simp; ring
    have hb : (1 - θ / (1 + θ)) / 4 ≤ θ / (1 + θ) := by
      rw [div_le_iff₀ (by norm_num : (0 : ℚ) < 4), sub_le_iff_le_add]
      have : 1 ≤ θ / (1 + θ) * 4 + θ / (1 + θ) := by
        rw [show θ / (1 + θ) * 4 + θ / (1 + θ) = 5 * θ / (1 + θ) by ring,
          le_div_iff₀ hpos]
        linarith
      linarith
    rw [e1, e2, max_self, max_eq_left hb, max_self]

/-- **The breakpoint is strict.** For `θ > 1/4`, *no* parameter choice reaches
`1/5`: the leg would then move the value, so it would be worth attacking. -/
theorem mleg_breakpoint (θ : ℚ) (hθ : 1 / 4 < θ) (a b : ℚ) : 1 / 5 < costM θ a b := by
  by_contra h
  push_neg at h
  have h1 : costExp a b ≤ 1 / 5 := le_trans (le_max_left _ _) h
  have h2 : θ * (1 - a) ≤ 1 / 5 := le_trans (le_max_right _ _) h
  obtain ⟨ha, -⟩ := costExp_unique_optimum a b h1
  rw [ha] at h2
  linarith

/-- **The real M-leg is co-tight.** At the unique optimum `a = b = 1/5`, the
actual leg `(N/r)^{1/4}` has exponent exactly `1/5`: it is active at the optimum,
yet deleting it does not move the value. Size, and even tightness, are not
leverage. -/
theorem mleg_cotight : (1 / 4 : ℚ) * (1 - 1 / 5) = 1 / 5 ∧
    ∀ a b : ℚ, costExp a b = 1 / 5 → (1 / 4 : ℚ) * (1 - a) = 1 / 5 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, fun a b h => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨ha, -⟩ := costExp_unique_optimum a b h.le
  rw [ha]; norm_num

/-- **The parametric value function** `V(θ) = max(1/5, θ/(1+θ))` for `θ ≥ 0`:
flat (redundant leg) up to the breakpoint `θ = 1/4`, then strictly increasing. -/
theorem mleg_value_function (θ : ℚ) (hθ : 0 ≤ θ) :
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x : ℚ × ℚ => costM θ x.1 x.2) (max (1 / 5) (θ / (1 + θ))) := by
  have hpos : (0 : ℚ) < 1 + θ := by linarith
  rcases le_total θ (1 / 4) with h | h
  · have : θ / (1 + θ) ≤ 1 / 5 := by
      rw [div_le_iff₀ hpos]; linarith
    rw [max_eq_left this]; exact mleg_value_of_le θ h
  · have : 1 / 5 ≤ θ / (1 + θ) := by
      rw [le_div_iff₀ hpos]; linarith
    rw [max_eq_right this]; exact mleg_value_of_ge θ h

/-! ## Which terms are load-bearing (over the box `0 ≤ a, b ≤ 1`) -/

/-- The parameter box `0 ≤ a ≤ 1`, `0 ≤ b ≤ 1` (`1 ≤ r, m ≤ N`). -/
def Box : Type := {x : ℚ × ℚ // 0 ≤ x.1 ∧ x.1 ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ x.2 ∧ x.2 ≤ 1}

/-- Delete the interior `N^{1/2}/(r^{1/2}m)`: value drops to `0`. -/
theorem delete_interior_value :
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x : Box => max x.1.1 x.1.2) 0 :=
  ⟨fun x => le_trans x.2.1 (le_max_left _ _),
    ⟨(0, 0), by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩, by simp⟩

/-- Delete the pair term `r`: value drops to `0`. -/
theorem delete_pairs_value :
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x : Box => max x.1.2 (1 / 2 - x.1.1 / 2 - x.1.2)) 0 :=
  ⟨fun x => le_trans x.2.2.2.1 (le_max_left _ _),
    ⟨(1, 0), by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩, by norm_num⟩

/-- Delete (make free) the baby-step term `m`: value drops to `0` — this is the
"free `m` is Lehman with a free `j`-loop" degenerate case. -/
theorem delete_babystep_value :
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x : Box => max x.1.1 (1 / 2 - x.1.1 / 2 - x.1.2)) 0 :=
  ⟨fun x => le_trans x.2.1 (le_max_left _ _),
    ⟨(0, 1 / 2), by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩, by norm_num⟩

/-- On the box, the three-term and four-term costs both have value `1/5`. -/
theorem box_full_value :
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x : Box => costExp x.1.1 x.1.2) (1 / 5) ∧
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x : Box => costM (1 / 4) x.1.1 x.1.2) (1 / 5) := by
  have hpt : (0 : ℚ) ≤ 1 / 5 ∧ (1 / 5 : ℚ) ≤ 1 ∧ (0 : ℚ) ≤ 1 / 5 ∧ (1 / 5 : ℚ) ≤ 1 := by
    norm_num
  refine ⟨⟨fun x => one_fifth_is_lower_bound _ _, ⟨(1 / 5, 1 / 5), hpt⟩, one_fifth_attained⟩,
    ⟨fun x => le_trans (one_fifth_is_lower_bound _ _) (le_max_left _ _),
      ⟨(1 / 5, 1 / 5), hpt⟩, ?_⟩⟩
  show max (costExp (1 / 5) (1 / 5)) (1 / 4 * (1 - 1 / 5)) = 1 / 5
  rw [one_fifth_attained]; norm_num

/-- **★ THE LOAD-BEARING CLASSIFICATION.** Of the four terms
`{interior, r, m, M}`, deleting any of the first three moves the value
(`1/5 → 0`), while deleting `M` leaves it at `1/5`. By the delete-a-term screen,
exactly three of the four terms carry the exponent; the M-leg is a co-leader only
in polylog weight. -/
theorem load_bearing_classification :
    (∃ x : Box, max x.1.1 x.1.2 < 1 / 5) ∧
    (∃ x : Box, max x.1.2 (1 / 2 - x.1.1 / 2 - x.1.2) < 1 / 5) ∧
    (∃ x : Box, max x.1.1 (1 / 2 - x.1.1 / 2 - x.1.2) < 1 / 5) ∧
    (∀ g' : Box → ℚ, ∀ x : Box, 1 / 5 ≤ max (costExp x.1.1 x.1.2) (g' x)) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := delete_interior_value.2; exact ⟨x, by simp only at hx; rw [hx]; norm_num⟩
  · obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := delete_pairs_value.2; exact ⟨x, by simp only at hx; rw [hx]; norm_num⟩
  · obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := delete_babystep_value.2; exact ⟨x, by simp only at hx; rw [hx]; norm_num⟩
  · exact (delete_a_term_screen (fun x : Box => costExp x.1.1 x.1.2) (1 / 5)).2
      (fun x => one_fifth_is_lower_bound _ _)

/-! ## The `m`-reuse is load-bearing -/

/-- **No baby-step split is Lehman.** With `m = 1` (`b = 0`), the exponent is at
least `1/3` for every `r`. -/
theorem no_split_is_lehman (a : ℚ) : 1 / 3 ≤ costExp a 0 := by
  simp only [costExp]
  rcases le_total a (1 / 3) with h | h
  · exact le_trans (by linarith) (le_trans (le_max_right _ _) (le_max_right _ _))
  · exact le_trans h (le_max_left _ _)

/-- ...and `1/3` is attained at `r = N^{1/3}`: Lehman's exponent exactly. -/
theorem no_split_value : costExp (1 / 3) 0 = 1 / 3 := by
  norm_num [costExp]

/-- **The baby-step term must be exactly balanced.** If `m ≠ N^{1/5}` then every
`r` gives cost strictly above `1/5`. -/
theorem babystep_must_balance (b : ℚ) (hb : b ≠ 1 / 5) (a : ℚ) : 1 / 5 < costExp a b := by
  rcases lt_or_eq_of_le (one_fifth_is_lower_bound a b) with h | h
  · exact h
  · exact absurd (costExp_unique_optimum a b h.symm.le).2 hb

/-- The collapse-coupling model: one Strassen-type product tree sweeps the joint
space `r × N^{1/2}/r^{1/2}` of size `N^{1/2}r^{1/2}` at square-root cost,
exponent `1/4 + a/4`, alongside the pair enumeration `a`. -/
def collapseExp (a : ℚ) : ℚ := max a (1 / 4 + a / 4)

/-- **The collapse coupling has optimum exactly `1/4`** over `r ≥ 1` (`a ≥ 0`). -/
theorem collapse_value :
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x : {a : ℚ // 0 ≤ a} => collapseExp x.1) (1 / 4) := by
  refine ⟨fun x => ?_, ⟨0, le_rfl⟩, by norm_num [collapseExp]⟩
  have := x.2
  exact le_trans (by linarith) (le_max_right _ _)

/-- **★ HEADLINE 2: the penalty is exactly `N^{1/20}`.** Removing the baby-step
split degrades the 3-term balance (`1/5`) to the 2-term collapse (`1/4`); the
penalty `1/4 - 1/5 = 1/20` is strictly positive, so the `m`-reuse is load-bearing. -/
theorem collapse_penalty :
    ∀ v w : ℚ, IsMinimaxValue (fun x : {a : ℚ // 0 ≤ a} => collapseExp x.1) v →
      IsMinimaxValue (fun x : ℚ × ℚ => costExp x.1 x.2) w → v - w = 1 / 20 := by
  intro v w hv hw
  rw [hv.unique collapse_value, hw.unique costExp_value]
  norm_num

/-! ## Screening the next target: the baby-step `m`-leg

The delete-a-term screen says `m` *is* worth attacking (deleting it moves the
value).  Here is what an attack on it would buy, computed exactly before any round
is spent on it. -/

/-- Harvey's balance with the baby-step leg discounted to `m^{1-ε}`. -/
def babyDiscountExp (ε a b : ℚ) : ℚ := max a (max ((1 - ε) * b) (1 / 2 - a / 2 - b))

/-- **Value of an `m`-leg discount.** If the baby-step list could be built in
`m^{1-ε}` (`0 ≤ ε < 1`), the optimum would be exactly `(1-ε)/(5-3ε)` — strictly
below `1/5` for every `ε > 0`, so this leg has genuine leverage. -/
theorem babyDiscount_value (ε : ℚ) (hε : ε < 1) :
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x : ℚ × ℚ => babyDiscountExp ε x.1 x.2) ((1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε)) := by
  have h1 : (0 : ℚ) < 1 - ε := by linarith
  have h5 : (0 : ℚ) < 5 - 3 * ε := by linarith
  refine ⟨fun x => ?_, ((1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε), 1 / (5 - 3 * ε)), ?_⟩
  · show (1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε) ≤ max x.1 (max ((1 - ε) * x.2) (1 / 2 - x.1 / 2 - x.2))
    set v := max x.1 (max ((1 - ε) * x.2) (1 / 2 - x.1 / 2 - x.2))
    have ha : x.1 ≤ v := le_max_left _ _
    have hb : (1 - ε) * x.2 ≤ v := le_trans (le_max_left _ _) (le_max_right _ _)
    have hi : 1 / 2 - x.1 / 2 - x.2 ≤ v := le_trans (le_max_right _ _) (le_max_right _ _)
    rw [div_le_iff₀ h5]
    nlinarith
  · show max ((1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε)) (max ((1 - ε) * (1 / (5 - 3 * ε)))
        (1 / 2 - (1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε) / 2 - 1 / (5 - 3 * ε))) = (1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε)
    have e1 : (1 - ε) * (1 / (5 - 3 * ε)) = (1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε) := by ring
    have e2 : 1 / 2 - (1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε) / 2 - 1 / (5 - 3 * ε) = (1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε) := by
      have key : (5 - 3 * ε)⁻¹ * (5 - 3 * ε) = 1 := inv_mul_cancel₀ h5.ne'
      linear_combination (-1 / 2 : ℚ) * key
    rw [e1, e2, max_self, max_self]

/-- Any genuine discount strictly beats `1/5`. -/
theorem babyDiscount_beats_fifth (ε : ℚ) (h0 : 0 < ε) (hε : ε < 1) :
    (1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε) < 1 / 5 := by
  rw [div_lt_div_iff₀ (by linarith) (by norm_num)]
  linarith

/-- Harvey's balance with the BSGS interior shrunk by `N^{-δ}`. -/
def interiorGainExp (δ a b : ℚ) : ℚ := max a (max b (1 / 2 - δ - a / 2 - b))

/-- **Value of an interior gain.** Shrinking the interior to `N^{1/2-δ}/(r^{1/2}m)`
gives optimum exactly `(1-2δ)/5 = (1/2-δ)/(5/2)`. -/
theorem interiorGain_value (δ : ℚ) :
    IsMinimaxValue (fun x : ℚ × ℚ => interiorGainExp δ x.1 x.2) ((1 - 2 * δ) / 5) := by
  refine ⟨fun x => ?_, ((1 - 2 * δ) / 5, (1 - 2 * δ) / 5), ?_⟩
  · show (1 - 2 * δ) / 5 ≤ max x.1 (max x.2 (1 / 2 - δ - x.1 / 2 - x.2))
    have ha : x.1 ≤ max x.1 (max x.2 (1 / 2 - δ - x.1 / 2 - x.2)) := le_max_left _ _
    have hb : x.2 ≤ max x.1 (max x.2 (1 / 2 - δ - x.1 / 2 - x.2)) :=
      le_trans (le_max_left _ _) (le_max_right _ _)
    have hi : 1 / 2 - δ - x.1 / 2 - x.2 ≤ max x.1 (max x.2 (1 / 2 - δ - x.1 / 2 - x.2)) :=
      le_trans (le_max_right _ _) (le_max_right _ _)
    linarith
  · show max ((1 - 2 * δ) / 5) (max ((1 - 2 * δ) / 5)
        (1 / 2 - δ - (1 - 2 * δ) / 5 / 2 - (1 - 2 * δ) / 5)) = (1 - 2 * δ) / 5
    have e : 1 / 2 - δ - (1 - 2 * δ) / 5 / 2 - (1 - 2 * δ) / 5 = (1 - 2 * δ) / 5 := by ring
    rw [e, max_self, max_self]

/-- **The flagged target `T = N^{(1/2-δ)/5}` is misstated by a factor of two.**
The correct value of an interior gain is `(1-2δ)/5 = 2·(1/2-δ)/5`; the proposed
formula is half of it for every `δ ≠ 1/2`, and at `δ = 0` it would claim `1/10`,
which `HarveyBalance.one_fifth_is_lower_bound` excludes. -/
theorem flagged_target_misstated (δ : ℚ) (hδ : δ ≠ 1 / 2) :
    (1 - 2 * δ) / 5 = 2 * ((1 / 2 - δ) / 5) ∧ (1 / 2 - δ) / 5 ≠ (1 - 2 * δ) / 5 := by
  refine ⟨by ring, fun h => hδ ?_⟩
  linarith

/-- At `δ = 0` the misstated formula undercuts the proven floor of the model. -/
theorem flagged_target_below_floor : (1 / 2 - 0 : ℚ) / 5 < 1 / 5 ∧
    ∀ a b : ℚ, (1 / 2 - 0 : ℚ) / 5 < costExp a b := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, fun a b => lt_of_lt_of_le (by norm_num) (one_fifth_is_lower_bound a b)⟩

/-- **Exchange rate of the two levers.** An `m`-leg discount `ε` and an interior
gain `δ` give the same exponent exactly at `δ = ε/(5-3ε)`: the discount `ε` is worth
the interior gain `δ = ε/(5-3ε)`. -/
theorem lever_exchange_rate (ε : ℚ) (hε : ε < 1) :
    (1 - 2 * (ε / (5 - 3 * ε))) / 5 = (1 - ε) / (5 - 3 * ε) := by
  have h5 : (5 - 3 * ε) ≠ 0 := by linarith
  have key : (5 - 3 * ε)⁻¹ * (5 - 3 * ε) = 1 := inv_mul_cancel₀ h5
  rw [eq_div_iff h5]
  linear_combination (-2 / 5 : ℚ) * ε * key

end Crypto.FactoringBarrier.DeleteATerm

# UMW correction: the constraint is `α ≥ 1−2β`, not `α+β ≤ 1` — plus a verified Lemma 6.2 construction

**Corrects #417 §6 and #418 §6.** Source opened in full (arXiv:2511.10851, ar5iv HTML);
all statements quoted verbatim. The round-33 synthesis and the main loop independently
reached the same "zero slack" conclusion, from the corrected boundary.

## The correction

**Conjecture 3.2 ((α,β)-Divisor Conjecture), verbatim:** "For infinitely many `n` there
exist subsets `S, T ⊆ ℤ⁺` such that the set of pairwise differences `A = {s−t ∣ s∈S, t∈T}`
satisfies the n-divisor property, and 1. all elements of `S,T` have magnitude at most
`exp(n^α)` 2. `|S|,|T| ≤ n^β`."

**The counting constraint, verbatim from the paper: `α ≥ 1 − 2β`.** The paper continues:
"we do not know if `α = 1−2β` is achievable. In fact, we do not even know if `α < 1−β` is
achievable (whereas `α = 1−β+o(1)` is trivial)."

⇒ The record (and #417) framed the trivial boundary as `α+β ≤ 1+o(1)`. That is the
**wrong** boundary. The trivial case is `α = 1−β+o(1)`; the counting obstruction is
**`α ≥ 1−2β`**. At the `α=β=1/3` target, `1−2β = 1/3 = α` **exactly** — zero slack.
This independently confirms (and now explains) the round-33 synthesis's "UMW's `1/6` is
its floor with zero slack": the deterministic-integer `1/5→1/6` consequence sits exactly
on the conjecture's counting wall.

## Lemma 6.2 (verified by execution)

"Let `U` be the product of primes in `[n]`. Given a factorization `U = U_1⋯U_ℓ`, define
`T_i` to be the multiplicative inverse of `U/U_i` (mod `U_i`), and `V_i = (U/U_i)T_i`.
There is an arithmetic progression `A = {b+ic : 1≤i≤ℓ}` containing multiples of each prime
in `[n]`, iff … `c·(Σ i·V_i) + b ≡ 0 (mod U)`."

Executed (`umw_lemma62.py`): enumerating 2-part factorizations of the primorial, a **2-term**
AP hits a multiple of every prime in `[n]` for several splits (verified for n = 10,15,20,25,30).
So the Lemma 6.2 construction is real and cheap. **But it is not the conjecture**: a 2-term
AP touches the *primes*, whereas Conjecture 3.2 needs the *difference set* of `S,T`
(each of size ≤ `n^β`) to divide-cover every `i ∈ [n]`. Assembling a full `(1/3,1/3)`
covering from the AP block is the open part — **not** obtained by this search.

## Lemma 6.3 (the generic obstruction, verbatim)

"Suppose for all positive integers `A_1,…,A_ℓ` with `A_i ≤ M` there exist `A'_1,…,A'_ℓ′`
in arithmetic progression, `A'_j ≤ M'`, such that for all `i` there exists `j` with
`A_i | A'_j`. Then either `ℓ′ ≥ M^{Ω(1)}` or `M' ≥ M^{log log M}`."
This rules out building the covering from an **arbitrary** partition of `[n]`. Only
**non-generic / structured** factorizations of the smooth integer escape it.

## Honest negative data point

A greedy/random set-cover search over disjoint `S,T ⊂ [1, e^{n^{1/3}}]`, `|S|=|T|=n^{1/3}`
(`umw_cover2.py`) gets coverage ≈ 0 at n = 64,128,256,512: a **random** `(1/3,1/3)`
construction does not cover. This is expected — the conjecture requires a **structured**
`S,T` — and is **not** evidence against UMW. It only shows any successful search must be
structural, not random.

## Status
UMW remains the one formally-open door (it acts on the index set `[n]`, the quantity the
whole campaign's `3/2`-barrier framing turns on). The exact open sub-problem, now stated
precisely: **for infinitely many n, construct structured `S,T` with `|S|,|T| ≤ n^{1/3}`,
elements ≤ `e^{n^{1/3}}`, whose difference set divides-covers `[n]`.** Lemma 6.2 supplies a
verified AP building block; Lemma 6.3 says only special factorizations of the smooth
integer can work. No such covering is constructed here.
